*This handout was written in Quarto and rendered to PDF with Typst. The
source is `handout/handout.qmd` in the project. Everything in it applies
to the document you are holding.*

# Getting in

Two doors, same room. Pick one. Switch if it does not work.

## Door 1: RStudio Desktop on your laptop

1. Open the project: double-click `IR-Quarto-Workshop.Rproj`.
2. Files pane (bottom right): `setup/00_install_packages.R`. Click **Source**. Wait for "Done".
3. `setup/01_check_setup.R`. Click **Source**. Ends with "Ready" or tells you what to fix.
4. `exercises/00_hello.qmd`. Click **Render**. A web page opens. You are in.

## Door 2: Posit Cloud, in a browser

1. Free account at **posit.cloud**.
2. Open the space link below. Click the project. Wait while it copies. Everything is installed.
3. `exercises/00_hello.qmd`. Click **Render**. You are in.

**Door 2 is for today's public data only.** Posit Cloud runs on servers
you do not control, hosted on AWS. Posit describes itself as a data
processor and will provide a data processing addendum on request, but we
found no public FERPA or SOC 2 statement for the Cloud product, and no
agreement between Posit and your institution exists unless your institution
made one. Student records do not go there without your own institution's
review and sign-off. The desktop stays on your machine, behind your
institution's controls. That is why it is the door you take home.

## Before anything else

**Your UNITID:** \_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_ (search `data/institutions.csv` by name; Auburn is 100858)

**An AI assistant you can log into:** ChatGPT, Claude, Copilot, Gemini. Any.

**If you are already in:** turn to "The STATS report" and start exercise 1. Do not wait.

## What you will leave with

A report about your own institution built from the Department of
Education's 2026 Program Performance Data, the preview of the earnings
accountability results that become official in February 2027. The code,
the data, the documentation, and the output are one file. When the official
file arrives, one script changes and your report re-renders.

# Why

**The problem.** More reports, more evidence, more dashboards, more
documentation. Same people. The production model has to change, not the
hours.

**The idea.** Put the query, the code, the explanation, the tables, the
charts, and the output format in one plain-text file. Render it. Version
it. Hand it over. Re-run it next year.

**The principle.** *The logic is readable; the data never is.* Everything
about how a number is made lives in a file anyone can read, including an AI.
Student records stay in the system of record and are read at render time.

## The landscape, and why these doors

| Where people are | Good at | Weak at |
|---|---|---|
| Excel, Access | one-off answers, familiarity | repetition, history, logic hidden in cells |
| Qlik, Tableau, Power BI | dashboards, drill-down | narrative, PDFs, documentation, version control; licensed per seat |
| SAS, SPSS, Stata | scripted analysis | the report is still assembled by hand; licensed |
| Jupyter, Colab, Databricks | Python exploration | publishing; Quarto renders notebooks too |
| VS Code, Positron | multi-language IDEs | newer; Positron is Posit's next IDE, worth watching |
| **RStudio Desktop** | free, stable, Quarto built in, one-button render, the IR community | needs an install |
| **Posit Cloud** | nothing to install; a browser | 1 GB on the free plan; cannot see your warehouse |
| Posit Workbench and Connect | the server versions: shared, scheduled, published | enterprise licenses |

## What Auburn did

For twenty years an Access database produced each year's college transfer
feedback reports. In 2026 the logic was read out of the VBA into plain
rules, re-implemented in Oracle and a Quarto template, and the old and new
systems were run on the same cohort and compared figure by figure. The
comparison matched, and found three errors the Access report had carried
for years. Then the Quarto template rendered one PDF per college, 46 of
them, in one run.

# What is inside RStudio

More than R. Point at this page during the tour.

## Languages, in the same document

| Chunk | Runs | Package |
|---|---|---|
| `{r}` | R | |
| `{python}` | Python | `reticulate` |
| `{sql connection=con}` | SQL against a live connection; result becomes a data frame | `DBI`, `odbc` |
| `{ojs}` | Observable JavaScript, interactive in the browser | |
| `{bash}` | shell | |

## Quarto output formats, one line each

`html` `typst` (PDF, nothing to install) `pdf` (LaTeX) `docx` `pptx` `revealjs`
`dashboard` `gfm` (GitHub) and whole websites, books, blogs, manuscripts.
Parameters. Conditional content per format. Cross-references. Citations
with Zotero. `brand.yml` for institutional colors, fonts and logo in one file.

## Packages worth knowing, by job

| Job | Packages |
|---|---|
| Wrangle | `dplyr`, `tidyr`, `janitor`, `stringr`, `lubridate` |
| Tables | `gt` (HTML, PDF, Word), `kableExtra` (PDF), `flextable` (Word, PowerPoint), `reactable`, `DT` (interactive) |
| Charts | `ggplot2`, `patchwork`, `ggrepel`, `plotly` (interactive), `leaflet` (maps) |
| Files | `readxl`, `writexl`, `openxlsx`, `haven` (SAS, SPSS, Stata), `jsonlite`, `httr2` (APIs) |
| Databases | `DBI`, `odbc`, `dbplyr` (write dplyr, get SQL), `keyring` (passwords out of files) |
| Office files | `officer` (build Word and PowerPoint from R) |
| Interactive | `shiny`, Shinylive (Shiny inside a static page) |
| Workflow | Projects, `renv` (lock versions), the Git tab, Terminal, Background Jobs, `styler`, `esquisse` |
| Higher ed | `educationdata` (IPEDS by API), `tidycensus`, `rscorecard`, `IPEDSuploadables` |
| AI | GitHub Copilot (built into RStudio; subscription), `ellmer` (call a model from code), `chattr` |

## Publishing

`quarto publish quarto-pub` (free, public). GitHub Pages. Netlify. Posit
Connect (licensed). Drop the HTML on SharePoint. Or what Auburn did: an
Azure static site behind campus sign-in, with a dashboard that shows each
person only the reports they may open.

## How IR offices use this

Fact books as websites. Program review profiles, one per department.
Course evaluation reports, one per instructor. Common Data Set and IPEDS
preparation. Accreditation narratives with the evidence tables embedded.
Survey reports from the Qualtrics API. Retention dashboards. Text analysis
of comments. Feedback reports to feeder institutions, one PDF each.

# The STATS report: exercises 1 to 3

## Exercise 1: your institution

1. Open `exercises/01_my_institution.qmd`.
2. Near the top, change `unitid: 100858` to your UNITID.
3. Click **Render**. Read it. Every number came from `data/`; every table
   and chart from a code chunk you can see.

Then look at the file. The YAML block at the top is settings. `params` is
the one thing that changes between institutions. Each grey block is a
chunk; `#| echo: false` hides the code from the reader. Everything else is
Markdown.

**Now click Source, then Visual.** The two buttons at the top left of the
editor. Same file, two views. Source is the plain text: the marks, the
fences, the YAML. Visual looks like a word processor: headings are big,
tables are grids, chunks are boxes. People write in Visual; an AI writes
Source, because Source is what it was trained on and what you paste into
it. Learn to read both. When an assistant hands you a chunk, you are
reading Source; when you fix the sentence above it, you are probably in
Visual. Nothing is lost switching, ever.

**Three verbs that are not the same thing.**

| Verb | Means | Where |
|---|---|---|
| **Run** | execute one chunk, or one line, in the Console, right now; the output appears below the chunk; nothing is written to disk | the green arrow on a chunk; Ctrl+Enter on a line |
| **Render** | execute every chunk from the top in a fresh session and build the output file (HTML, PDF, Word) | the Render button; `quarto render` in the Terminal |
| **Publish** | copy a rendered output somewhere other people can open it | `quarto publish`; or drop the file on a server, SharePoint, the portal |

Run is for thinking. Render is for the document. Publish is for the
audience. A chunk that Runs but does not Render was depending on something
in your session that the document never loaded; Render is the test.

## Exercise 2: the same report, four ways

Change the `format:` block and Render each time. Change it back after.

| Want | Write |
|---|---|
| Word | `format: docx` |
| PDF | `format: typst` |
| Slides | `format: revealjs` |
| All three at once | list them, then in the Terminal tab: `quarto render exercises/01_my_institution.qmd` |

Notice the last section, "Every current program", is missing from the PDF.
In the file it is wrapped in `::: {.content-visible when-format="html"}`.
Long tables for the web, short ones for paper, one source.

## Exercise 3: five institutions, one click

1. Open `exercises/03_render_peers.R`.
2. Edit the list of names and UNITIDs. Change `format` if you want PDFs.
3. Click **Source**. Five reports appear in `output/`.

This is the whole trick behind one-PDF-per-college, one-report-per-
department, one-profile-per-program. The template does not know how many
there are.

## Exercise 6: the IPEDS pattern (for later, or for the fast)

1. Open `templates/ipeds/EF_fall_enrollment.qmd`. Render it. It runs on
   3,000 invented students, so it works anywhere.
2. Read one question section: the IPEDS question quoted, the rule in
   prose, the chunk, the answer. Four pieces, every question.
3. Find the checks section. Change a rule so a check fails. Render. It
   refuses. That refusal is the feature.

`docs/ipeds-tutorial-for-cecile.md` explains the pattern: one population
query, many small question chunks, checks that stop the render, an upload
file written by the last chunk, and the year as a parameter. Replace the
fake-data chunk with your census query and the rest stays.

## If it breaks

| Message | Means |
|---|---|
| `No programs found for unitid` | typo, or your campus reports under a parent OPEID; search `institutions.csv` by name |
| `could not find function` | a package is not loaded; add `library(...)` in the setup chunk |
| `object 'x' not found` | a chunk above did not run; Render runs them in order from the top |
| the PDF table is cut off | shorten column labels or drop a column; or keep it HTML-only |

# The data, and exercise 4

## What PPD:2026 is

Published by the Department of Education in December 2025, updated January
8, 2026, for the AHEAD negotiated rulemaking. One row per **institution ×
credential level × 4-digit CIP**: 209,321 programs at 5,096 institutions.
A preview, for information only. The official results under STATS (the
Student Tuition and Transparency System, from the One Big Beautiful Bill
Act) arrive **February 2027** at the 6-digit CIP level.

## The tables in `data/`

| File | One row per | Use for |
|---|---|---|
| `ppd_programs.rds` | program | today: earnings, debt, benchmark, pass/fail, completer demographics |
| `ppd_yearly.rds` | program × award year | 2015-16 to 2024-25: enrollment, completers, Pell, every loan type |
| `ppd_institution_yearly.rds` | institution × year | in-state and out-of-state Title IV enrollment |
| `ppd_cip6_earnings.rds` | program at 6-digit CIP | the earnings detail the official file will use |
| `institutions.csv` | institution | find a UNITID; compare institutions |
| `codebook.csv` | column | every column, what it means, where it came from |

## Three things to know before computing anything

1. **NA means suppressed, not zero.** Fewer than 10 students (16 for
   earnings, 30 for FAFSA-based columns) is blanked. Sums undercount.
2. **Counts of 10 to 19 are shown as 15.** Rates built on them use 15.
3. **The dollars are different years.** Earnings and benchmarks: 2024
   dollars. Debt: 2019 dollars. Yearly aid: nominal.

## The test, in one line

`md_earn_wne_p4` (median earnings of completers working four years after
the 2017-18 and 2018-19 cohorts) against `earn_bnchmrk_cip2_wageb` (high
school graduates aged 25 to 34 in the state for undergraduate programs;
bachelor's holders in the field for graduate programs). Below it:
`earnings_test = "Fail"`.

## Exercise 4: daydream

Pick one; add a section to your report. Code for six of them is in
`solutions/04_daydream_examples.qmd`.

Who is within 10% of the line, either side. Which benchmark each program
was held to. Ten years of Pell share. Loan volume by year, Parent PLUS vs
Grad PLUS. Non-completion by program, trended. Debt against earnings, one
point per program. The same program at five peers. Pass and fail across
your whole state by control. Completer demographics against results.
Delinquency and default for the one cohort that has it. Your programs at
6 digits. The one-page Typst brief for the provost.

# Asking an AI, safely

```{=typst}
#block(width: 100%, inset: 10pt, fill: rgb("#FFF4EC"), stroke: 1pt + rgb("#E87722"), radius: 4pt)[
  #text(weight: "bold", size: 12pt)[The rule: share the shape of the data, never the rows.]
  #v(0.4em)
  Column names, types, a description, the codebook: yes. Student records: never. Small aggregates can identify people: think first. Passwords and keys: never. \
  Today's dataset is public and has no student-level data, so you may paste rows from it. That is the exception. Your warehouse is not like this.
]
```

## Prompt 1: describe, then ask

> I am writing a Quarto report in R using dplyr, ggplot2 and gt. I have a
> data frame `tested`, one row per academic program, with these columns:
> *[paste lines from codebook.csv]*. Write one R chunk that *[what you
> want]*. Use `theme_minimal()`. Do not install packages. Return only the chunk.

## Prompt 2: the error

> Here is my R chunk: *[chunk]*. Here is the error: *[the red text]*. What
> is wrong and what is the fix?

## Prompt 3: make it say something

> Here is a table of results: *[5 to 15 rows]*. Write three sentences for a
> provost that state the main finding plainly, with no adjectives, and
> name the one program that most needs attention.

Treat the answer as a draft. Check every number.

## Prompt 4: the report you actually owe someone

> I produce *[report]* for *[audience]* every *[cadence]*. Today I build it
> in *[tool]* by *[steps]*. The data has these columns: *[names and types,
> no rows]*. Outline a Quarto document that produces it, with a parameter
> for *[what changes each time]*, and list the chunks I would need.

## What the assistant is good and bad at

Good: syntax you forgot, a first draft of a chunk, explaining an error,
turning a table into sentences, suggesting a chart. Bad: knowing your
data, knowing your rules, arithmetic you did not check, anything it cannot
see. It will produce confident code that runs and is wrong. Rendering is
the test; reading is the second test.

## With an API key (optional)

The `ellmer` package calls a model from an R chunk, so a summary paragraph
can be written at render time. Costs money per call. Key in `keyring`,
never in a file. Same rule applies: whatever is in the data frame you pass
leaves the building.

# Cheat sheet, and taking it home

## The top of a Quarto file

```yaml
---
title: "Report"
date: today
format:
  html:
    toc: true
    embed-resources: true     # one file, images inside
params:
  unitid: 100858
execute:
  echo: false                 # hide code from readers
  warning: false
---
```

## In a chunk

```r
#| label: name          # unique; shows in Render progress
#| fig-height: 4
#| echo: true           # show this one chunk's code
```

## Markdown you will use

`# Heading` `## Subheading` `**bold**` `*italic*` `` `code` `` `[text](url)`
`1. list` `- bullet` `| a | b |` for tables, `::: {.callout-note}` for a box,
`` `r params$unitid` `` for a value inside a sentence.

## Render many

```r
quarto::quarto_render("report.qmd", execute_params = list(unitid = 100858),
                      output_file = "Auburn.html")
```

## Connect to your own warehouse (desktop only, at home)

Not in Posit Cloud. See the note under Door 2.

```r
con <- DBI::dbConnect(odbc::odbc(), dsn = "MY_DSN",
                      UID = "my_user", PWD = keyring::key_get("my_service", "my_user"))
df  <- DBI::dbGetQuery(con, "SELECT ... FROM ...")
```

`MY_DSN` is an ODBC data source your IT office sets up on your machine.
Set the password once in the Console: `keyring::key_set("my_service", "my_user")`.
It is stored by the operating system, not in any file, and never in a
document like this one.

## February 2027

The official STATS file will arrive at 6-digit CIP with its own layout.
In this project, `ingest/make_ppd_tables.R` is the one file that reads the
Department's files. Change it; every report re-renders.
